# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system using a phased rollout. Both systems will run in parallel (dual-write / shadow-run capable) throughout the migration, allowing rollback of any individual user or batch back to the legacy system without data loss. The legacy system remains fully operational and authoritative for unmigrated users at every phase; no decommissioning of the legacy system occurs until a separate, subsequent decommission phase after all migration phases are complete and verified.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full integration testing in staging, including reconciliation testing against a mirrored copy of production billing data with 100% ledger match on a sample of at least 5,000 synthetic transactions; on-call rotation and rollback tooling (single-user and batch rollback to legacy) have been tested end-to-end and signed off by Engineering and Finance.

**Scope:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in, low-risk external users (e.g., free-tier or low-transaction-volume accounts) selected to minimize blast radius. No enterprise or high-ARR accounts included.

**Duration:** 1 week minimum observation before proceeding.

**Activities:** Migrate accounts, run dual-write reconciliation daily, validate invoicing, payment capture, refunds, proration, and tax calculation against legacy outputs.

---

## Phase 2: Early Adopters / Broad Cohort (25% of users — ~10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full observation window with zero unresolved critical (Sev1/Sev2) billing defects, invoice discrepancy rate in Phase 1 stayed below 0.1% of migrated invoices, and Finance has signed off on reconciliation reports for the pilot cohort.

**Scope:** A representative cross-section of the user base by plan type, geography, and payment method (cards, ACH, wallets, invoiced enterprise-lite), excluding the highest-ARR/most contractually sensitive accounts, which are reserved for Phase 3.

**Duration:** 2 weeks minimum, migrated in sub-batches of ~2,500 users every 2–3 days to allow monitoring between waves.

**Activities:** Continue dual-run reconciliation, expand monitoring dashboards to cover payment failure rates, dunning/retry behavior, and customer support ticket volume tagged "billing."

---

## Phase 3: General Availability / Remaining Users (73% of users — ~29,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 sustained an invoice discrepancy rate below 0.1%, payment failure rate delta versus legacy system below 0.5 percentage points, zero unresolved Sev1 incidents for 10 consecutive days, and support ticket volume attributable to billing migration has remained flat or declining week-over-week.

**Scope:** All remaining users, including enterprise, high-ARR, and contractually sensitive accounts, migrated last given their complexity and business risk.

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks, migrated in weekly waves of roughly 7,000–10,000 users, with enterprise accounts migrated individually with dedicated customer success involvement and a scheduled maintenance window per account where required by contract.

**Note:** The legacy billing system remains fully live, supported, and unmodified throughout Phase 3. Decommissioning, disabling, or deleting the legacy system is explicitly out of scope for Phase 3 and is deferred to a separate Phase 4 (Legacy Decommission) that begins only after all 40,000 users are confirmed migrated and a minimum 30-day parallel-run/cool-down period has elapsed with no rollback events.

---

## Rollout Halt Metric

The rollout will be automatically paused (no further batches migrated) if the **invoice discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5% of migrated invoices in any rolling 24-hour window**, or if **payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds legacy system's baseline failure rate by more than 2 percentage points** in any rolling 24-hour window. Either threshold breach triggers an immediate freeze, root-cause investigation, and Finance/Engineering joint sign-off before resuming.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missed charges due to dual-write race conditions between old and new systems | Implement idempotency keys and a reconciliation job that compares ledgers hourly during overlap, alerting on any mismatch | Engineering Lead (Billing Platform)
RISK: Payment method tokenization mismatch causes failed charges after migration | Pre-validate token migration in a shadow run against the payment processor's sandbox for every batch before cutover | Payments Engineering Owner
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms (custom proration, discounts, invoicing schedules) are misconfigured in the new system | Require manual contract-term verification and customer success sign-off for every enterprise account prior to migration in Phase 3 | Enterprise Customer Success Lead
RISK: Regulatory/tax calculation differences between systems lead to incorrect tax collection in certain jurisdictions | Run parallel tax calculations for all migrated invoices for the first 30 days and require Finance/Tax team sign-off before scaling batch size | Finance/Tax Compliance Owner
RISK: Rollback of a batch from new system back to legacy system causes data loss or duplicate billing events | Build and test an automated rollback runbook per batch with a dry-run requirement before every phase, verified against sandbox data | Site Reliability Engineering Owner

PHASES: 3
